source.snippet: I am administrator of Organisation One. I want to be able to share my account's mailbox with my Microsoft 365 Business Basic account in Organisation Two, like one can with a shared mailbox. Is this possible? I ask because with GMail, it is, via account delegation.

problem_statement: IT admins who manage multiple Microsoft 365 tenants cannot natively share or delegate mailbox access across tenant boundaries, forcing manual workarounds or duplicate accounts — a gap that Gmail handles natively via account delegation.
target_segment: IT administrators and small business owners managing two or more separate Microsoft 365 tenants (e.g. parent/subsidiary, freelancer with multiple clients)
notes: Buyer signal: paying M365 Business Basic subscriber, explicitly referencing a workflow available in a competing paid product (Gmail delegation). The gap is structural in Microsoft's architecture; a connector service or managed-identity bridge could be sold to IT-managed SMBs. Single signal but the pain is a known class of M365 complaint — moderate signal strength pending volume confirmation.
